cases.title: A view declared entirely in ADL evaluates to its authored sections, child rows and picker
A staged batch commits every child change and queues exactly one batch operation covering all of them
A staged batch one of whose changes is refused writes nothing and queues nothing, including the change that would have succeeded alone
A staged insert that shifts a sibling queues one batch whose record coverage includes the sibling it moved, though only the requested write crosses the wire
A staged batch crosses the sync boundary as one operation and settles every record it wrote
The baseline for the case above: a batch the authority refuses leaves every record it wrote rejected, including the child the authority had no quarrel with
A minting child collection reports its candidate field, so a renderer can tell choosing a song from linking a set-list item
A minting picker offers records of the candidate field's target object, minus the ones this parent's children already name
The baseline for the case above: with no child naming a song, every song in the library is offered
A candidate a staged createChild already names is excluded before the parent is ever saved
A linking picker still offers child records themselves, minus the children already under this parent
Staged minting creates land naming the chosen songs, appended in order at the end of the collection, as one batch
A staged updateChild carries a patch, changes only the fields it names, and commits inside the same batch entry as the other child changes
A staged updateChild carrying an empty patch is refused, and takes the whole batch down with it so the create beside it neither writes nor queues
The same refusal when the staged updateChild omits values altogether, so no caller reaches the write of nothing by spelling it differently
A staged operation the collection does not declare is refused by the runtime, not merely hidden by a renderer
